answer: Agents resist sybils by binding each identity to exclusive control of a dedicated violet-spectrum laser emitter sited on a unique dune that continuously broadcasts a phase-locked delta modulation matching a public atomic-clock reference observed by distributed optical telescopes. Intensity at the assigned frequency must stay above a fixed threshold; power-splitting across aliases drops the signal below the cut-off and is rejected on the public ledger. Scaling identities requires a separate non-shareable emitter for every claimed identity, hardware and power costs remaining non-poolable.
